# PR 12788 retrospective

The narrow three-file integration and explicit third-party trust boundary were reviewable without hardware. Independent source review challenged low-value optional feedback and avoided turning a recovery inconvenience into a finding quota. Separate source-derived flow and test limits keep the public outcome proportionate.

Opus expanded into a compact stub experiment, whose retained per-case outputs are useful but whose blanket guard claims were too strong. The coordinator read the whole driver and inventory, requested a preserved audit addendum, and accepted only individual source-supported results. No rerun was justified solely to improve a broad PASS count. Future fixtures must gate every log producer and assert intermediate targets; private TMPDIR is containment only. Archive members must be read before extraction, not reconstructed afterward.

Sequential policy reads should be mandatory in dispatches; the stated aggregate bound was violated by parallel reads once. Preserve native output/history rather than hiding the incident. A direct coordinator guidance redirection also omitted the centralized path assertion; use the path helper for every generated artifact.

No-extension Pi starts suppress Herdr session hooks. Verify the native session header after its first neutral assignment rather than treating missing startup hook metadata as a model failure. Keep prior sessions preserved and record this compatibility limitation. Auto-memory was disabled for Claude; process-only startup context was disclosed. No prior technical conclusions were imported.

No Omadev/toolkit product bug confirmed. Potential tooling improvement: encode target/producer checklist acceptance and expected native-session-file readiness in the launcher. Do not let those implementation gaps idle technically sound reviews once required evidence and editorial gates pass.
comment:
**Verified:** No important actionable defect found in the first-party AirPods integration at `246590e`. Source inspection confirms that installation requires consent before package/plugin setup, and removal preserves the plugin checkout if its uninstaller fails.

The inspected removal path is:

```text
Confirm removal
  -> plugin uninstaller
       -> release device guard
       -> stop/remove service
  -> remove plugin checkout (only after uninstaller succeeds)
```

This is a source-derived sequence, not a hardware result. The linked project's release-first ordering was inspected at `68d3a87`; later upstream versions may differ.
